title: Affinity evaluation ordering bug causes silent tenant tier swap during heavy reclaim
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: During a high-utilization reclaim window (midnight UTC, Mar 1), a race in the affinity policy evaluation path caused multiple tenants to be silently reassigned from higher-tier Dedicated pools to lower-cost Hosted/compat variants. This resulted in increased latency and degraded output quality for several enterprise customers for ~18 minutes before an automated rollback and manual mitigation were applied. The misassignment was deterministic under a specific ordering of policy snapshots and an eviction-triggered recompute path that bypassed the tie-break stabilizer.
reproduction_steps: 1) Create two policy snapshots with identical priority and overlapping region affinity for tenant T-827 in Dedicated and Hosted tiers.
2) Simulate capacity reclaim: mark GPUs as under eviction and trigger tenant eviction handler.
3) Concurrently push a policy update that reorders affinity rules for the tenant (snapshot TTL < 5s).
4) Observe resulting route: evaluation chooses the lower-tier variant due to non-deterministic iteration order and missing canonical tie-break during recompute.
5) Run integration repro harness with 500 parallel requests across 3 regions to reproduce rate of misroutes consistent with production incident.
investigation_summary: Investigators (Sergio, Mei, Jonah) traced request traces to the routing-evaluator process. Logs showed that when the eviction handler invoked a 'fast-recompute' path, it used a policy map iterated with default hash order. Meanwhile, the stable tie-break key (region-priority-timestamp) was only applied in the full snapshot path, not in the fast path. Under concurrent policy pushes, the fast path committed earlier and produced a lower-rank selection. Telemetry indicates ~42k requests affected, with latency P95 increasing from 180ms -> 560ms for impacted tenants.
root_cause: A fast-recompute code path introduced to reduce latency during eviction omitted the canonical tie-breaker used by the normal evaluation flow. The omission combined with non-deterministic hash-map iteration and near-simultaneous policy snapshot updates created a deterministic bias toward lower-cost variants under load. The fast path was merged last quarter with optimistic assumptions and lacked a unit test for deterministic selection under concurrent updates.
mitigation: 1) Emergency rollback: disable fast-recompute path via runtime flag (done at 2026-03-01T00:18Z) => immediate reversion to canonical flow.
2) Applied tenant-level fixes for the three highest-affected customers: pinned them to Dedicated until patch verified.
3) Increased policy snapshot TTL to 30s temporarily to reduce churn while patch is being validated.
4) Added an alert on rate of tier swaps per tenant (threshold: 5 swaps / 5m).
fix_plan: Short term (hotfix): Reintroduce canonical tie-breaker in fast-recompute code path and add deterministic iteration over policy list. Ship as runtime-1.20.1 with unit and integration tests.
Medium term: Add concurrency tests in routing-evaluator CI that simulate concurrent policy pushes + eviction windows.
Long term: Rework policy snapshot merge semantics to make fast-recompute fully feature-compatible with full-eval, or deprecate fast path if parity cannot be guaranteed.
rollout_plan: 1) Publish hotfix build to staging and run tenant-sim cluster for 4 hours with high churn workload (QA + Canary).
2) Canary rollout to 5% of production traffic across low-risk tenants for 2 hours; monitor tier-swap and latency metrics.
3) Gradual ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 6 hours if no regression.
4) After full rollout, revert temporary policy TTL increase and unpin customers.
qa_plan: - Unit tests for deterministic tie-break ordering in both fast and full eval paths.
- Integration test harness that runs 1k parallel policy updates + eviction events and asserts zero incorrect tier swaps over 30 runs.
- Manual verification with affected customers in a private staging slice.
